root_cause.text: In `nf_conntrack_helper_unregister()`, passing NULL instead of the helper pointer to `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy()` prevented the removal of associated connection tracking expectations, allowing them to dereference the freed helper object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the change from `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, NULL)` to `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, me)`, and the CVE description states that passing NULL caused `expect_iter_me()` to fail matching expectations, leaving them alive when the helper object was subsequently freed, triggering a slab-use-after-free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes helper unregistration to correctly scope expectation destruction to the specific helper instance rather than passing NULL.

intent_record.how: Ensures the expectation destruction iterator receives the specific helper context, allowing it to filter and destroy only expectations associated with the helper being unregistered.

candidates.rationale: This statement passes NULL to nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(), which prevents the destruction of connection tracking expectations associated with the specific helper being unregistered. Consequently, these expectations retain references to the freed helper object, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement passes NULL as the second argument to nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(), which prevents the function from properly destroying connection tracking expectations associated with the specific helper instance. When the helper is subsequently freed, these orphaned expectations still hold references to it, creating a use-after-free vulnerability when they attempt to dereference the freed helper object.
